talks.title: Qing Yang - Im A Newbie Yet I Can Hack ZigBee
talks.teaser: A beginner-accessible exploration of ZigBee radio communication, sniffing packet traffic, and exploiting vulnerabilities in smart lighting.
talks.summary:
Overview of the ZigBee Protocol in IoT Ecosystems

Qing Yang of Qihoo 360's Unicorn Team introduces the fundamentals of ZigBee (IEEE 802.15.4), a low-power wireless mesh networking standard widely deployed across smart lighting, home automation, smart meters, and industrial sensors. The talk provides a practical roadmap for security researchers entering the realm of IoT hardware and radio analysis.

Firmware Extraction and Key Recovery

Yang demonstrates hardware reverse engineering workflows on commercial ZigBee devices. By tapping serial flash memory chips and debugging interfaces like JTAG and UART, the researcher extracts device firmware images and analyzes disassembled code to locate hardcoded default network encryption keys and pre-shared master keys.

Packet Sniffing and Wireless Command Injection

Using software-defined radios and inexpensive ZigBee sniffer hardware, the presentation details capturing wireless association handshakes and decoding transmitted payloads. Yang demonstrates sniffing keystrokes from wireless controllers, forging valid network frames, and injecting unauthorized control packets to manipulate smart door locks and connected switches.

Securing Embedded ZigBee Implementations

The briefing underscores critical defensive recommendations for IoT device manufacturers. Manufacturers must avoid shipping well-known default trust center link keys, enforce encrypted over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates, and protect debug interfaces against physical probing.
